owner_posts.post_text:
Taxpayers registered under the Composition Scheme are required to furnish GSTR-4 for Financial Year 2025-26 within the prescribed due date.

The return contains details relating to turnover, tax liability, and taxes paid during the financial year.

Timely filing supports smooth GST compliance and record maintenance.

Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a vital role in economic growth, employment generation, innovation, and entrepreneurship.

International MSME Day recognizes the contribution of small businesses in strengthening local economies and driving sustainable development.

Supporting MSMEs contributes to a stronger and more resilient economy.

Taxpayers registered under the QRMP Scheme are required to deposit GST liability for May 2026 through Form PMT-06, wherever applicable.

PMT-06 is used for payment of tax and other applicable dues under GST by eligible quarterly return filers.

Timely payment assists in maintaining GST compliance and avoiding interest implications.

Registered taxpayers required to file monthly GST returns should ensure timely filing of GSTR-3B for May 2026.

GSTR-3B contains a summary of outward supplies, input tax credit claimed, and net GST liability for the tax period.

Timely filing and payment help maintain compliance under GST provisions.

GST Update – West Bengal
As per Notification No. 02/2026-C.T./GST dated 22.05.2026, generation of an E-Way Bill has become mandatory for intra-state movement of goods within West Bengal where the consignment value exceeds ₹50,000, except for movement related to job work.

The notification is effective from 01.06.2026. Businesses should ensure timely compliance and update their internal processes and ERP systems accordingly to avoid disruptions in the movement of goods.

Did You Know? Proper Record Retention Matters. Maintaining financial and tax records for the prescribed period is an important aspect of compliance under the Income-tax Act, 1961 and GST laws.

Well-organized documentation can assist in:
✔️ Responding to Income Tax scrutiny proceedings
✔️ Addressing GST notices, assessments, and audits
✔️ Supporting income, expense, and deduction claims
✔️ Retrieving historical records whenever required

Whether you are an individual taxpayer, business owner, professional, firm, or company, maintaining accurate records can help ensure smoother compliance and reduce difficulties during verification processes.

Quarterly TDS certificates relating to payments other than salary for the quarter ended March 2026 are due for issuance.

These certificates assist deductees in verifying taxes deducted and claiming corresponding tax credit.

Accurate and timely issuance helps reduce reconciliation issues at the time of return filing.

ITR Filing FY 2025-26 (Non-Audit Cases): Document Checklist for Businesses, Professionals, Firms & LLPs Preparing the right documents in advance can help ensure accurate and timely filing of Income Tax Returns.

Key information generally required may include:
✔️ Basic KYC and banking details
✔️ Business or professional income records
✔️ GST reconciliations (where applicable)
✔️ House property and home loan documents
✔️ Capital gains details from shares, mutual funds, property, and other assets
✔️ Interest, dividend, and other income details
✔️ Investment and deduction proofs under eligible provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961

Early compilation of records helps minimize reconciliation issues, reporting errors, and last-minute compliance challenges.

Employers are required to issue TDS certificates relating to salary income and tax deducted during Financial Year 2025-26 within the prescribed timeline.

The certificate serves as an important document for employees while preparing and verifying their income-tax returns.

Timely issuance promotes smooth tax compliance and reconciliation.

The first instalment of Advance Tax for Tax Year 2026-27 falls due on 15 June 2026.

Advance tax provisions are designed to distribute tax payments throughout the year and reduce year-end tax burdens.

Taxpayers with estimated tax liability may evaluate their advance tax obligations in advance of the due date.

The update is straightforward but important: all Income Tax Return (ITR) forms for AY 2026–27 have now been officially notified. What this really means is the compliance framework for the upcoming filing cycle is in place, and taxpayers can expect filing to open soon on the portal.

The notification covers the full set of forms—ITR-1 and ITR-4 for individuals with simpler income structures, ITR-2 and ITR-3 for more complex cases, and ITR-5, 6, and 7 for firms, companies, and trusts. It also includes ITR-V for verification and ITR-U for updated returns. These will apply to income earned during FY 2025–26.

For anyone filing this year, this is your signal to start preparing documents, reviewing income sources, and avoiding last-minute chaos.

TDS on partner interest is now clearly defined under Section 194T, and timing matters more than most people think. If interest is credited or paid to partners, TDS needs to be deducted at the earlier of the two. For March 2026, the deposit deadline is 30th April 2026. Missing this isn’t just a delay, it can trigger interest and compliance issues.

The latest Income Tax update brings much-needed clarity on the applicability of GAAR (General Anti-Avoidance Rules) to legacy investments. The CBDT has now clearly stated that investments made before 1st April 2017 will not fall under GAAR provisions, even if gains arise in subsequent years.
What this really means is that investors holding pre-2017 structures can breathe easier. The grandfathering benefit continues, ensuring that genuine investments made in the past are not questioned under anti-avoidance regulations. This removes a major area of ambiguity that had been creating concern, especially among foreign investors.
From a practical standpoint, this amendment draws a clear line between legitimate legacy investments and aggressive tax planning arrangements. It reduces the risk of unnecessary scrutiny and litigation while reinforcing trust in India’s tax framework.
For businesses and investors, this is a positive signal. Policy clarity like this not only improves compliance but also strengthens investor confidence and long-term planning.
